answerToTheQuestionAsked: The question was whether the public mempool rejects an RSA-2048 DKIM frame while the alt mempool admits it. It does not: at 61,330 gas the check fits inside the 100,000 validation-prefix cap, so the canonical public mempool accepts it and mines it. No alt mempool, no staking, is needed for DKIM.

optimisation.why: The first version compared EM byte by byte. Indexing bytes memory bounds-checks every access, and indexing a bytes constant copies the whole constant on each access, so 253 comparisons cost about 180k gas. Checking EM as eight 32-byte words instead costs almost nothing. The MODEXP precompile itself is only 5,461 gas by EIP-2565 (multiplication_complexity 1024, iteration_count 16).

notable: This transaction carried signatures: [] - no signature entries at all. Authorisation came only from the DKIM signature checked inside the VERIFY frame.
negativeTest: One bit flipped at byte 200 of the signature: rejected before inclusion, 'validation prefix frame reverted'. The same tampered signature returns false from the standalone verify() view.
altMempool: Accepted the tx and then never included it, the same defect seen in 5a.
